// Part: room: entrance hall (interior furnisher + lamplighter). Inner air x45..50, z43..60, y4..9 (rooms.json box).
// The grand stair (x45..46, z54..60) is the stair joiner's, already built: its foot and rising flight stay clear.
// Layout: a red runner down the centre lane x47..48 to the stair; two console tables with a pot and a candle flank the
// front door; a dark-oak settee (stairs as seats) on each side wall; a coat rack (fence post + lantern) in the NE corner;
// standing lanterns on fence posts at the back corners; two hanging lanterns down the centre line under the upper hall.
import { B, layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";

const ORIGIN_X = 45;
const ORIGIN_Z = 43;

const LEGEND = {
  C: "red_carpet",
  P: "dark_oak_planks",
  F: "dark_oak_fence",
  s: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "west", half: "bottom" }],
  e: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "east", half: "bottom" }],
  c: "flower_pot",
  k: ["candle", { candles: "1", lit: "true" }],
  L: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
};

// x45..50 per row, z43..60 down the rows ('.' = nothing here)
const FLOOR_Y4 = [
  "..CC.F", // z43 coat rack foot, carpet
  "P.CC.P", // z44 console tables
  "..CC..", // z45
  "..CC..", // z46 parlour door x44 and dining door x51 stay clear
  "..CC..", // z47
  "F.CC..", // z48 lamp post against the west wall
  "s.CC.e", // z49 settees against the side walls
  "s.CC.e", // z50
  "..CC..", // z51 corridor doors stay clear
  "..CC..", // z52
  "......", // z53
  "......", // z54 stair steps at x45..46 (not drawn here)
  "......", // z55
  ".....F", // z56 lamp post, NE of the stair
  "......", // z57
  "......", // z58
  "....F.", // z59 lamp post by the wing opening
  "......", // z60 wing opening lane x47..50
];

// rows by z (43..60): every row not named is free
const rowsAt = (named) => Array.from({ length: 18 }, (_, i) => named[43 + i] ?? "......");

const Y5 = rowsAt({
  43: ".....F", // coat rack
  44: "c....k", // pot on the west console, candle on the east one
  48: "L.....", // standing lantern on the west lamp post
  56: ".....L", // standing lantern on the fence post
  59: "....L.", // standing lantern on the fence post
});

const Y6 = rowsAt({ 43: ".....F" }); // coat rack, top post
const Y7 = rowsAt({ 43: ".....L" }); // coat rack lantern on top

export function build(g) {
  layers(g, [ORIGIN_X, 4, ORIGIN_Z], LEGEND, FLOOR_Y4);
  layers(g, [ORIGIN_X, 5, ORIGIN_Z], LEGEND, Y5);
  layers(g, [ORIGIN_X, 6, ORIGIN_Z], LEGEND, Y6);
  layers(g, [ORIGIN_X, 7, ORIGIN_Z], LEGEND, Y7);

  // hanging lanterns down the centre line, under the upper hall ceiling (y10 is solid for z43..49)
  for (const z of [44, 48]) {
    g.set(47, 9, z, ...B.chain("y"));
    g.set(47, 8, z, ...B.lantern(true));
  }
}

input.summary:
parts/room-1.mjs (entrance hall) is unchanged: its 42 writes all fall inside the shell's interior air, so runParts refuses every one and nothing is placed.
Palette is clean (no OFF-PALETTE lines for this part). The fix is upstream: the shell fills interior air, which runParts counts as owned.
make.sh still writes build.nbt, but this part's REFUSED line remains.

waste.what: Worked out by hand that the 42 refusals are every write in the part (30 floor cells, 6 at y5, 1 at y6, 1 at y7, 4 for the two chains and lanterns) and that they all sit in the shell's owned interior air box x45..50 z43..60 y4..9.
waste.cost: Counted 42 writes by reading the layers rows; about 4 source reads and 3 greps to trace the lock
waste.tool: runParts could print an owned-cell census per part (owned air vs owned solid, and which earlier part owns each region) so a furnishing part can see at once that its whole box is shell air; a `mcd plan`-style check for 'every target cell owned' would have flagged this before make.sh

waste.what: Traced the root cause by hand: runParts adds every cell an earlier part writes to `owned`, including air, and shell.mjs fills the interior with 'air' (box() and the fill helper), so the room box is locked. A fresh Grid is already air, so those air fills add ownership and no content.
waste.cost: About 6 tool calls to read build.mjs runParts, shell.mjs and check Grid's default block
waste.tool: runParts could treat air placed over a fresh grid's default air as unowned (or report it as 'air-only ownership'); a lint in `mcd check` for 'part writes air where the grid is already air' would point at shell.mjs directly

left: REFUSED 42 remains: every write in parts/room-1.mjs lands in air the shell already placed, and no cell in the room box is free, so there is no move that keeps the furnishing. The fix belongs to the shell or to runParts, which I was told not to edit.

Root cause: parts/shell.mjs fills interior air (box() around line 27, and the carve/open helpers), and build library runParts (/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs ~l.243) adds every earlier-written cell, air included, to `owned`. A fresh Grid already reads minecraft:air, so those air fills only create ownership. Suggested fix, for the shell owner: don't write air into interior cells (only carve where a non-air block was placed), or have runParts skip air-only ownership.
Bypassing the lock inside room-1 (writing to the underlying grid) would have hidden the conflict, so I did not do it.
Other room parts (room-2..room-37) are still stubs that write nothing, but they sit under the same owned air and will hit the same refusal once written.

OFF-PALETTE: none for this part. Blocks used: red_carpet, dark_oak_planks, dark_oak_fence, dark_oak_stairs, flower_pot, candle, lantern, iron_chain, all in palette.json. The off-palette lines in make.sh output are roof.json's (tuff_brick*, cobbled_deepslate_*, polished_deepslate_*, stone_brick_slab), which belong to the roofs part, not room-1.

Root cause: parts/shell.mjs fills interior air (box() around line 27, and the carve/open helpers), and build library runParts (/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs ~l.243) adds every earlier-written cell, air included, to `owned`. A fresh Grid already reads minecraft:air, so those air fills only create ownership. Suggested fix, for the shell owner: don't write air into interior cells (only carve where a non-air block was placed), or have runParts skip air-only ownership.
Bypassing the lock inside room-1 (writing to the underlying grid) would have hidden the conflict, so I did not do it.
Other room parts (room-2..room-37) are still stubs that write nothing, but they sit under the same owned air and will hit the same refusal once written.
